name: A19 one-formula candidate T26 (MOGF0IE, w = 0.1): paper rule + published Moster halo mass for gas-poor galaxies above M_t + halo floor; no contraction; baryons of spheroids with a measured dispersion carry the observed IMF trend
frozen_at: 2026-11-07 01:20 PST, session SA73 overnight, after the T24 to T26 cross-validations
halo_formula: M_ref = Mp/fb + 10^A (M*/1e10 Msun)^B (Re/3 kpc)^C + q M_Moster(M*, z), q = (M*/Mp)^50 / (1 + (M_t/M*)^4); M_halo = (M_ref^8 + (1e8 Msun)^8)^(1/8); M_Moster: Moster, Naab and White (2013) with redshift evolution, inverted in [1e9, 10^16.5] Msun; NFW with dark mass (1-fb) M_halo inside r200 at the halo redshift, log10 c = 0.520 + 0.385 exp(-0.617 z^1.21) + (-0.101 + 0.026 z) log10(M_halo h/1e12 Msun) (Dutton and Maccio 2014), satellites x (1 - 0.54 log10(D/r200,host)) (Moline et al. 2017); no contraction; fb = 0.049/0.3175, h = 0.671; lensing M_p as a point mass
baryons: stellar g_bar of spheroids with a measured velocity dispersion x alpha_IMF = 10^(0.38 log10(sigma_e/200 km/s) - 0.06 + 0.215) (Posacki et al. 2015 trend relative to Salpeter; Chabrier scale via Madau and Dickinson 2014); used for the 50 MaNGA BCGs (<sigma_los>, Tian et al. 2024) and the 16 SPARC early types (sigma_e, Cappellari et al. 2013a); stellar masses in the halo formula stay on the published Chabrier-like scale
coefficient_count: 4 (A, B, C set on disks alone; log10 M_t from the joint fit)
caveats: adaptive: fourteenth round on seen data, not blind
the early types' inner points are ATLAS3D JAM values, which Posacki et al. used, so they do not test the IMF trend independently; their outer HI points get 1.6 percent worse
systems without a measured dispersion (CLASH BCGs, KiDS lenses) keep the published baryons
status: retrospective and adaptive; frozen here for a blind test on new systems
